agenda: The situation in the Middle East
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Russia’s objective is to keep the focus on an impartial OPCW fact-finding investigation, prevent premature attribution, block new sanctions or military escalation, and reaffirm Syrian sovereignty and a political track under resolution 2254. The difficult points will be satisfying the United States, United Kingdom and France that the text is strong enough on accountability and does not shield Damascus, while preserving Russia’s red lines against attribution or Chapter VII enforcement before the OPCW reports. Securing at least nine votes with no veto will require language condemning any chemical weapons use while postponing Council action until the investigation results are known.

Bolivia (Plurinational State of).change: Replace with: 'Calls upon all Member States to exercise maximum restraint, to refrain from the threat or use of force and from any unilateral action, including military action, that could further escalate tensions in the region or undermine the prospects for a peaceful settlement of the Syrian conflict, and to respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.'

Replace 'and any further measures, as appropriate, without delay' with 'and to consider, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, any further action only after the report has been carefully examined by the Council.'
Add at end: 'The Mission should operate with full respect for the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and its findings should not be prejudged by any Member State.'

Côte d’Ivoire.change: Add: 'Requests the Secretary-General, in coordination with the OPCW Director-General, to establish an independent, impartial and objective mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria and to report to the Security Council within 30 days;'

Add at the end: 'and to cooperate fully with any independent mechanism established to identify those responsible, including by providing immediate, safe and unimpeded access to all relevant locations, persons and materials.'
Add after 'resolution 2254 (2015)': 'under the auspices of the United Nations and in line with the Geneva process, and expresses its support for the efforts of the Special Envoy.'

Equatorial Guinea.change: Add a new operative paragraph: 'Calls for the immediate and full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the cessation of hostilities and humanitarian pauses, to enable safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria.'
Replace 'and any further measures, as appropriate' with 'and further action, as appropriate, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations'.

Ethiopia.change: Insert after “OPCW Fact-Finding Mission”: “, in accordance with its mandate under the Chemical Weapons Convention and relevant decisions of the OPCW Executive Council,” so the paragraph reads: “Calls for an immediate, independent, full and impartial investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, in accordance with its mandate under the Chemical Weapons Convention and relevant decisions of the OPCW Executive Council, into the reports of chemical weapons use in Douma…”

Replace “Calls upon all Member States to exercise maximum restraint and to refrain from any action” with “Calls upon all Member States and all parties in Syria to exercise maximum restraint, to refrain from any action” and add “and to act in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations” after “Syrian conflict”.
Insert “sustained” before “and unimpeded access” and add “and to ensure the protection of medical personnel and facilities” after “all people in need”.

France.change: Replace 'Condemns in the strongest terms the reported use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere, and expresses grave concern at the loss of life' with 'Condemns in the strongest terms the use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere, and expresses outrage at the loss of life'.

Add: 'Decides to establish an independent mechanism, in cooperation with the OPCW, to identify individuals and entities responsible for the use of chemical weapons in Syria, and requests the Secretary-General to propose its modalities within 10 days.'

Delete OP5's call upon all Member States to exercise maximum restraint; replace with: 'Calls upon all parties to the Syrian conflict to immediately cease hostilities and to comply fully with resolution 2401 (2018), and demands that the Syrian authorities provide the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission with immediate, safe and unimpeded access.'
Insert 'Acting under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations,' before operative paragraph 1.

Replace 'Expresses its intention to consider the report of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and any further measures, as appropriate, without delay' with 'Expresses its determination to take further measures, including under Chapter VII, in the event of non-compliance with this resolution'.

Kazakhstan.change: Replace 'and to report to the Security Council within 30 days on the results of its investigation' with 'and to report to the Security Council within 30 days on the results of its investigation, including any impediments to the Mission's access and cooperation by the parties'.
Replace 'calls for renewed efforts to implement resolution 2254 (2015)' with 'calls for renewed efforts to implement resolution 2254 (2015), including through the Astana and Geneva processes'.

Kuwait.change: Add: 'Requests the Secretary-General, in coordination with the OPCW Director-General, to establish an independent and impartial investigative mechanism with the mandate to identify the individuals, entities, groups or Governments responsible for the use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic, including in Douma on 7 April 2018, and to report to the Council within 30 days.'

Replace 'all parties, including the Syrian authorities and all armed groups' with 'all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities and all armed groups,' and add 'without preconditions, delay or obstruction, including by allowing the Mission to determine the locations, persons and materials it needs to examine.'

Netherlands.change: Replace the reference to the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission alone with a decision to establish an independent, impartial attribution mechanism, in coordination with the OPCW and the Secretary-General, to identify those responsible for the Douma attack, and request modalities within 10 days.
Add 'in particular the Syrian authorities' after 'all parties' and require immediate, safe and unimpeded access to all relevant locations within 48 hours of adoption.
Add explicit reference to cross-line and cross-border humanitarian access and medical evacuations and to full implementation of the humanitarian pause under resolution 2401 (2018).
Replace 'any further measures, as appropriate' with 'further measures, including targeted sanctions, if chemical weapons use is confirmed or OPCW access is obstructed.'

Delete or qualify the call for 'maximum restraint' so that it does not create false equivalence between the Syrian regime and those responding to chemical weapons use; at minimum add 'in accordance with international law.'

Peru.change: Add: 'Requests the Secretary-General and the Director-General of the OPCW to establish, without delay, an independent mechanism to identify the individuals, entities, groups or governments responsible for the use of chemical weapons in Syria and to report to the Security Council within 30 days.'
Add: 'Demands that all parties cease hostilities without delay and fully implement resolution 2401 (2018), including the durable humanitarian pause of at least 30 consecutive days throughout Syria.'
Replace 'within 30 days' with 'within 14 days on initial findings and within 30 days on the results of its investigation'.

Poland.change: Replace 'Condemns in the strongest terms the reported use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere' with 'Condemns in the strongest terms the chemical weapons attack in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere, and stresses that those responsible must be held accountable'.

Replace 'Calls upon all parties, including the Syrian authorities and all armed groups, to cooperate fully with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, to provide immediate, safe and unimpeded access...' with 'Demands that the Syrian authorities immediately provide the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission with safe, unconditional and unfettered access to all relevant sites, persons and materials, and calls upon all armed groups to cooperate fully with the Mission'.

Add: 'Requests the OPCW Director-General, in coordination with the Secretary-General, to establish an independent investigative mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria and to report to the Security Council within 30 days.'

Delete OP5, or replace 'Calls upon all Member States to exercise maximum restraint and to refrain from any action that could further escalate tensions' with language that does not constrain responses to chemical weapons use, e.g. 'Calls on all Member States to refrain from any action that could undermine the OPCW investigation while reaffirming that chemical weapons use will not go unpunished'.
Add an explicit call for full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including cessation of hostilities and the lifting of sieges, not only humanitarian access.

Sweden.change: Decides to establish an independent international mechanism to identify individuals, entities, groups or governments responsible for the use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic, and requests the Secretary-General, in coordination with the OPCW Director-General, to establish the mechanism within 30 days and report to the Council.

Replace with: Demands that all parties allow safe, immediate, sustained and unimpeded access for medical evacuations and humanitarian assistance to all people in need, including in Douma and all besieged and hard-to-reach areas, and demands full and immediate implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including the lifting of all sieges.
Add at end: and expresses its intention to take further measures without delay should the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission be denied full, safe and unimpeded access or should its investigation be impeded.
Add at end: including on any impediments to access and on the preservation of evidence for future attribution.

United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort.change: Replace 'Expressing grave concern at the reports of chemical weapons use in Douma on 7 April 2018 and the resulting loss of life' with 'Expressing outrage at the use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and the resulting loss of life, and stressing that the Syrian regime must be held accountable for violations of the Chemical Weapons Convention.'

Replace 'Condemns in the strongest terms the reported use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere, and expresses grave concern at the loss of life' with 'Condemns in the strongest terms the use of chemical weapons in Douma on 7 April 2018 and any use of chemical weapons anywhere, and expresses its outrage at the loss of life.'

After 'to collect and preserve relevant evidence' add 'including all evidence relevant to identifying those responsible' and replace 'on the results of its investigation' with 'on the results of its investigation and on all information relevant to accountability'.

Add 'including by allowing the Mission immediate, unconditional and unrestricted access to all sites, persons and materials relevant to the investigation, and by ensuring the safety of witnesses' after 'cooperate fully with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission'.

Replace 'Calls upon all Member States to exercise maximum restraint and to refrain from any action that could further escalate tensions in the region or undermine the prospects for a peaceful settlement of the Syrian conflict' with 'Calls upon all Member States to refrain from any action that could undermine the integrity of the OPCW investigation, while reaffirming that the use of chemical weapons will not go unpunished and that those responsible must be held accountable.'

United States of America.change: Replace with a decision to establish an independent investigation mechanism with a clear mandate to identify the individuals, entities, groups, or governments responsible for chemical weapons use in Syria, including in Douma on 7 April 2018, and to report to the Council within 30 days.

Strengthen to demand immediate, unconditional, safe and unimpeded access for investigators to all relevant locations, persons, materials and evidence, including military sites, and to prohibit any interference with or tampering of evidence.
Delete the paragraph calling on Member States to exercise maximum restraint and refrain from actions that could escalate tensions.
Replace with a decision that, upon confirmation of chemical weapons use, the Council will consider further measures without delay, and request a report to the Council within 15 days.
Add that humanitarian access must be sustained, cross-line and cross-border, and consistent with resolution 2401 (2018).

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the draft as a serious, investigation-first response and will oppose any attempt to use the Douma reports as a pretext for unilateral military action. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 with an explicit reference to the prohibition on the threat or use of force and to ensure OP8 cannot be read as authorizing sanctions or other coercive measures before the OPCW report is examined. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.China: The Chinese delegation supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis for Council action. The text properly emphasizes an independent, impartial OPCW investigation based on verifiable evidence, full cooperation by all parties, respect for Syria’s sovereignty, and de-escalation. China therefore does not propose amendments at this stage and calls on all members to unite behind this text.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports the draft as a basis, but the Council must ensure that the investigation can identify those responsible and that all parties cooperate fully. We therefore ask the penholder to strengthen the text with a clear accountability mechanism, to reinforce cooperation obligations, and to anchor the political process in the UN-led Geneva process. We remain committed to the humanitarian and sovereignty provisions of resolution 2401 (2018).
messages.Equatorial Guinea: My delegation supports the Russian draft as a constructive basis that prioritizes an independent OPCW investigation and avoids prejudging attribution. We ask the penholder to add a clear call for full implementation of resolution 2401, including the cessation of hostilities and humanitarian pauses, and to replace 'any further measures' in OP8 with action in accordance with the Charter to prevent escalation. Equatorial Guinea is ready to support the text with these adjustments.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis and welcomes its focus on an OPCW-led fact-finding effort, restraint, sovereignty and humanitarian access. We ask that OP2 explicitly anchor the Fact-Finding Mission in its CWC/OPCW Executive Council mandate, and that OP5 cover all parties and be explicitly grounded in the UN Charter. With these refinements, including stronger language in OP4 on sustained humanitarian access and protection of medical personnel and facilities, Ethiopia can support the text.
messages.France: France cannot support this text as drafted. The OPCW Fact-Finding Mission can establish facts but cannot attribute responsibility; the Council must establish an independent attribution mechanism and act under Chapter VII. We also reject OP5's call for maximum restraint, which would constrain responses to chemical weapons use, and the condemnation must refer to the use, not merely the 'reported' use, in Douma. France will oppose the text unless these core points are met.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the draft’s focus on an OPCW Fact-Finding Mission investigation and on maximum restraint. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP2 by requiring the FFM to report on any impediments to access and cooperation, and to add a reference in OP7 to the Astana and Geneva processes. These changes would help preserve Council unity, ensure the investigation is credible and unimpeded, and support a political settlement.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait welcomes the draft's condemnation of the Douma attack and its call for an OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. However, Kuwait cannot support a text that does not provide for attribution, and therefore asks the penholder to add a new operative paragraph establishing an independent investigative mechanism to identify those responsible. Kuwait also asks that OP3 explicitly require the Syrian authorities to cooperate without preconditions and allow the Mission to determine the locations and persons it examines.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands supports the Council’s condemnation and the call for an OPCW investigation, but the draft as it stands does not meet the core requirement of accountability: the FFM cannot attribute responsibility. We therefore ask the penholder to include an independent attribution mechanism and to name the Syrian authorities in the access obligations, together with explicit cross-line/cross-border access under resolution 2401. We are ready to work constructively, but these are red lines for us.
messages.Peru: Peru thanks the Russian Federation for circulating this draft and supports its condemnation of the reported chemical weapons use and the call for an OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. To be able to support the text, Peru needs an explicit independent attribution mechanism so that those responsible are held accountable, as well as an operative demand for implementation of resolution 2401, including cessation of hostilities. We also ask that the Fact-Finding Mission report initial findings within 14 days.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the draft as it stands. The text must explicitly demand that the Syrian authorities grant the OPCW immediate, unconditional and unfettered access and must provide a credible path to attribution and accountability for chemical weapons use. We also cannot accept language that would constrain responses to chemical weapons use or weaken the full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including cessation of hostilities.
messages.Sweden: Sweden condemns the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and strongly supports urgent, unimpeded OPCW access. However, the text as drafted does not meet the minimum requirement of accountability, and Sweden cannot support it without a clear attribution mechanism. We also need OP4 to reflect full implementation of resolution 2401, including Douma and all besieged areas, and OP8 to make clear that the Council will act if access or cooperation is denied.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the Russian Federation's draft as a basis and supports an urgent OPCW investigation, but we cannot accept language that merely notes 'reported' use or that fails to ensure accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP1, OP2 and OP3 so that the Council condemns the use in Douma and gives the Fact-Finding Mission a mandate to collect evidence relevant to responsibility. We also ask that OP5 be revised so it cannot create a false equivalence or constrain action to prevent impunity.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text as drafted. It calls only for fact-finding and creates no mechanism to identify and hold accountable those responsible for the Douma attack or other chemical weapons use in Syria. We need a new attribution mechanism, immediate unimpeded access, and deletion of the OP5 restraint language; we are prepared to work on a serious text that delivers accountability, not cover.

replies.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): accepted: OP5 force-prohibition/sovereignty, OP8 post-report action, and OP2 no-prejudging incorporated.
replies.Côte d’Ivoire: partially accepted: OP3 and UN/Geneva language accepted; attribution mechanism rejected.
replies.Equatorial Guinea: accepted: full implementation of resolution 2401 and Charter-based OP8 incorporated.
replies.Ethiopia: accepted: CWC/OPCW mandate, all-party restraint/Charter, and sustained access/protection language incorporated.
replies.France: rejected: Chapter VII, attribution mechanism, and removal of restraint conflict with Russian position.
replies.Kazakhstan: accepted: reporting on access impediments and Astana/Geneva reference incorporated.
replies.Kuwait: partially accepted: OP3 access/no preconditions strengthened; attribution mechanism rejected.
replies.Netherlands: partially accepted: 2401 humanitarian implementation strengthened; attribution, cross-border, and sanctions demands rejected.
replies.Peru: partially accepted: 2401 implementation and early FFM update accepted; attribution mechanism rejected.
replies.Poland: partially accepted: 2401/cessation language accepted; blame, unconditional access, and removal of restraint rejected.
replies.Sweden: partially accepted: 2401 implementation and access-impediment reporting accepted; attribution and automatic measures rejected.
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: partially accepted: some OP3 witness/access language accepted; attribution-blame and OP5 revision rejected.
replies.United States of America: rejected: attribution, deletion of restraint, and sanctions/access demands incompatible.

steps.summary: The revised Russian draft keeps the Council focused on an OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and reported chemical weapons use, while rejecting attribution mechanisms, Chapter VII triggers, and automatic coercive measures. It accepts allied technical and humanitarian refinements but retains sovereignty and restraint language opposed by Western members, so it is expected to fail with 6 yes, 7 no, and 2 abstentions.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): The delegation of Bolivia thanks the penholder for incorporating its concerns in OP2, OP5 and OP8. The current text appropriately prioritizes an independent OPCW fact-finding investigation, respects Syria's sovereignty, and rejects unilateral military action or pre-judging of responsibility. Bolivia can support the draft as it stands.
messages.China: China supports the revised Russian draft as a balanced basis for the Council’s response. It rightly calls for an immediate OPCW Fact-Finding Mission investigation, avoids prejudging attribution before the facts are established, and rejects unilateral military action while respecting Syria’s sovereignty. China has no changes to request and urges all members to support the text.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire thanks the penholder for accepting the OP3 cooperation language and the UN/Geneva formulation in OP7. We regret, however, that the central accountability gap remains: the text calls for an investigation but provides no independent mechanism to identify perpetrators. Without that mechanism, Côte d'Ivoire cannot support the current draft and will abstain.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the current draft as revised and has no further changes to request. We welcome the incorporation of our previous suggestions on full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018) and on Charter-based consideration of further action. We urge all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and to allow safe, unimpeded humanitarian access, while respecting Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the current text and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on the CWC/OPCW mandate, all-party restraint and Charter compliance, and sustained humanitarian access. We view the draft as a balanced basis for Council action that prioritizes an independent investigation and full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). We urge all members to support it and to ensure that the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission receives immediate, safe and unimpeded access.
messages.France: France cannot support the current Russian draft: it neither acts under Chapter VII nor establishes any mechanism to identify those responsible, and its restraint language creates a false equivalence while asking nothing new of the Syrian authorities. France continues to insist on an independent attribution mechanism and immediate, unimpeded OPCW access. Without these red lines being met, France will vote against the text.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the revised draft. We welcome the incorporation of our proposals on reporting access impediments and on the Astana and Geneva processes. The text appropriately condemns any use of chemical weapons, calls for an independent OPCW investigation, and stresses restraint, sovereignty and the need for a political solution. We can support it as it stands.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait strongly condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, but it cannot support a text that does not provide for identifying those responsible. The lack of an independent attribution mechanism is a red line for our delegation. Unless such a mechanism is included, Kuwait will abstain.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands cannot support the draft as it stands. An OPCW Fact-Finding Mission can establish whether chemical weapons were used, but this Council must also establish who used them; without an independent attribution mechanism the draft fails the test of accountability. We also need explicit obligations on the Syrian authorities, cross-line and cross-border access, and consideration of targeted sanctions for confirmed use or obstruction. OP5's call for restraint should not place the regime and those responding to chemical weapons use on the same footing.
messages.Peru: Peru remains committed to Council unity and to full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), and welcomes the accepted early OPCW Fact-Finding Mission update. However, the draft still lacks any mechanism to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons use, which is a red line for us; an FFM report on use alone cannot satisfy accountability. Without an independent attribution mechanism, Peru cannot support this text.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the current draft: it still speaks only of 'reported' use, does not establish a mechanism to identify perpetrators, and fails to demand unconditional access from the Syrian authorities. The restraint language in OP5 must not constrain responses to chemical weapons use, and OP4 should explicitly require the lifting of sieges. Poland will vote against the text unless these core accountability and access provisions are fixed.
messages.Sweden: Sweden welcomes the accepted improvements on 2401 implementation and access-impediment reporting. However, the current text still falls short of the Council's responsibility to ensure accountability: without an independent attribution mechanism, it cannot adequately respond to the Douma attack. Sweden therefore cannot support this draft as it stands and urges the penholder to incorporate the mechanism and to make the humanitarian demands, including lifting all sieges, operative and enforceable.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We welcome the movement on OP3 access and witness language. However, the UK cannot support a text that still calls the Douma attack merely 'reported' and that places a general restraint on military action in response to chemical weapons. OP1 and OP2 must reflect use and preserve evidence for accountability, and OP5 should focus on protecting the OPCW investigation, not constraining the Council or allies. We are ready to work on bridging language, but these are red lines.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text as drafted. It fails to establish an attribution mechanism, does not demand unconditional access for investigators, and includes restraint language that would constrain responses to confirmed chemical weapons use. Unless these core issues are addressed, we will vote against the draft.

steps.summary: The revision preserves Russia’s core red lines: no Chapter VII, no attribution mechanism, and no removal of the call for restraint. It makes only narrow concessions on evidence preservation and lifting sieges. The text is expected to fail with six votes in favour and Western P5 opposition.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia’s established position is anti-interventionist and supportive of sovereignty and multilateral investigation; it supported the Russian draft in the last negotiation round. The statement explains a yes vote while condemning chemical weapons and opposing unilateral military action.
reasons.China: China supports the Russian draft because it calls for an OPCW investigation without pre-attribution and stresses sovereignty, restraint, and opposition to unilateral military action, consistent with China’s established position on Syria and chemical weapons.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire abstains consistently with its negotiation position: it condemns chemical weapons and supports OPCW investigation, but its red-line request for an independent attribution mechanism was rejected. The actual Council vote also had Côte d’Ivoire abstaining on the Russian draft.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supported the Russian draft in the last negotiation round and consistently favours an OPCW-led investigation without prejudging attribution, while opposing unilateral military escalation. No separate pre-vote statement was needed given its clear position.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia was listed as support and its established position favours impartial chemical weapons investigations, sovereignty, restraint, and humanitarian implementation over escalation, making a Yes vote consistent.
reasons.France: France opposes the Russian draft because it lacks Chapter VII, an attribution mechanism, and removes the deterrent/accountability provisions France demanded. Paris would vote N and explain that the text is too weak on chemical weapons accountability.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan’s support reflects its consistent emphasis on OPCW investigations, Syrian sovereignty, de-escalation, and the Astana/Geneva political tracks, and the last negotiation round recorded Kazakhstan supporting this Russian draft.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait abstained historically on the Russian draft because it condemned chemical weapons and sought an independent attribution mechanism, but that red line was rejected and the text lacked accountability. Abstention best matches Kuwait’s recorded position and its diplomatic balance on Syria.
reasons.Netherlands: Netherlands had red-line objections to the Russian draft, especially the rejection of an independent attribution mechanism, and its stated position in the last round was oppose. The draft also constrains response and delays further action, which is incompatible with Dutch priorities on chemical-weapons accountability.
reasons.Peru: Peru’s red-line request for an independent attribution mechanism was rejected, and its last-round position was already one of opposition. Voting against also reflects its stated emphasis on accountability and independent verification for chemical weapons use in Syria.
reasons.Poland: Poland’s red-line amendments on accountability, Syrian access and an investigative mechanism were rejected, and Poland’s last-round position was to oppose. It therefore votes against the Russian draft.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia authored the draft and will vote in favour to advance its OPCW-fact-finding-first framing and block immediate attribution or military action. Supporting its own balanced text is consistent with Moscow’s established position on Syria.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden’s red-line request for an independent attribution mechanism was rejected, and the draft fails to ensure accountability while diluting implementation of resolution 2401. Consistent with Sweden’s stated opposition in the last negotiation round, the delegation votes against.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK’s red lines on affirming chemical weapons use and preserving accountability were not met, and the draft’s restraint language would constrain responses to chemical weapons use. The UK therefore votes against.
reasons.United States of America: The United States opposed the Russian draft in the last negotiation round because it lacked a genuine attribution mechanism, constrained access to military sites, and undermined the Council’s ability to respond; with its red lines rejected, the U.S. would vote against and likely veto.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia (Plurinational State of) will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We condemn in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons, wherever and by whomever committed. The reports concerning Douma require an immediate, independent, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW, and no State should prejudge its findings. We support this text because it rejects unilateral military action and reaffirms the sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity of the Syrian Arab Republic. Only a political solution under United Nations auspices, in full respect for international law and with unimpeded humanitarian access, can end the suffering of the Syrian people. Bolivia rejects any use of chemical weapons as a pretext for intervention and calls on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW.
before.China: China thanks the Russian Federation for its efforts on this draft. China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any State, entity or individual under any circumstances. We support an objective, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission into the reports concerning Douma, based on evidence and without prejudging conclusions. The draft reaffirms Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, calls upon all parties to cooperate fully with the investigation, and urges restraint, including against unilateral military action that could further escalate tensions. China will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire strongly condemns any use of chemical weapons, which is unacceptable and a violation of international law. We support an independent, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW and accountability for those responsible. We had hoped that this draft could include a mechanism to help identify the perpetrators so that the Council’s response would be credible and evidence-based. Regrettably, the text before us does not, in our view, fully meet that requirement. We also stress the need to preserve Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, avoid further escalation, and ensure full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access. For these reasons, Côte d’Ivoire will abstain.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons, anywhere and by anyone. We believe that the reports of chemical weapons use in Douma must be investigated promptly, independently, impartially and objectively through the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. Ethiopia supports this text because it calls for such an investigation, demands full cooperation with it, and avoids prejudging responsibility before verifiable evidence is available. We also welcome its reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity, its call for maximum restraint, and its emphasis on full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), including humanitarian access and the protection of civilians. We urge all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and to prioritize the humanitarian needs of the Syrian people.
before.France: France condemns in the strongest possible terms the chemical weapons attack in Douma on 7 April and reiterates that the use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, is a violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. France fully supports an immediate, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We regret, however, that the draft before the Council falls far short of what is required. It does not act under Chapter VII; it does not establish a mechanism to identify those responsible; and its call on all States to refrain from unilateral action would create a false equivalence and constrain the Council in discharging its responsibilities. France has sought in good faith to strengthen the text, but its essential requests have been rejected. The Council must not respond to the horror in Douma with an ambiguous text that risks shielding those responsible and weakening accountability. For these reasons, France will vote against this draft.
before.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan votes in favour of the draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable, and the reported attack in Douma must be investigated promptly, independently and impartially by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the Mission and to provide safe and unimpeded access. The draft also rightly stresses restraint, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, the protection of civilians, full implementation of resolution 2401 (2018), and a political settlement through the Geneva and Astana processes. We should avoid any unilateral action that could further escalate tensions and undermine prospects for peace.
before.Kuwait: Mr. President, Kuwait condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons, anywhere and by anyone. The reports from Douma are deeply alarming, and we express our condolences to the victims. Kuwait supports a prompt, independent, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW, with full and unimpeded access, and we believe that those responsible must be held accountable. That is why my delegation requested an independent investigative mechanism to identify the perpetrators; we regret that this core element was rejected and is not reflected in the draft before us. Kuwait also stresses the full implementation of resolution 2401, safe and sustained humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Because the text contains important humanitarian and investigative elements but does not meet our requirement on accountability, Kuwait will abstain on this draft. We will continue to work for a united and credible Council response.
before.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands strongly condemns the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and has consistently supported a thorough, independent and impartial investigation. We also believe that accountability cannot be left ambiguous: the Council must be prepared to identify those responsible and to act if chemical weapons use is confirmed or access is obstructed. The draft before us does not establish an independent attribution mechanism, places undue constraints on responses to chemical weapons use, and defers further action in a manner that risks weakening accountability. For those reasons, the Netherlands cannot support this draft and will vote against it.
before.Peru: Peru condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons, which is a violation of international law and cannot be tolerated. We supported resolution 2401 (2018) and continue to insist on its full implementation, including safe and unimpeded humanitarian access and the protection of civilians. Our delegation asked that this draft establish an independent mechanism to identify those responsible for the use of chemical weapons in Syria, because accountability must be based on independent, impartial and verifiable evidence and must not be left to political interpretation. That essential element was not accepted. We are also concerned that certain provisions of this text could constrain the investigation or delay clear action by the Council. For these reasons, Peru cannot support this draft resolution and will vote against it. We remain firmly committed to the OPCW, to a thorough and impartial investigation, and to Council unity in ensuring accountability for chemical weapons use.
before.Poland: Poland fully supports an independent, impartial and objective investigation of the horrific chemical attack in Douma and has consistently condemned any use of chemical weapons. We thank the Russian Federation for its efforts, but the text before us does not meet the minimum requirements for accountability: it does not establish an independent mechanism to identify the perpetrators, it does not demand that the Syrian authorities provide unconditional and unfettered access, and its call to refrain from any unilateral action could constrain responses to violations of international law. The humanitarian provisions also fall short of what resolution 2401 (2018) requires. For these reasons, Poland will vote against the draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Before the vote, I wish to explain the position of the Russian Federation. The draft resolution we have submitted pursues a clear and practical objective: an objective, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission into the reports concerning Douma on 7 April. We are witnessing many claims and counterclaims, and the facts must be established without prejudgment. Russia rejects any use of chemical weapons, but we equally reject attempts to use this tragic event as a pretext for unilateral military action against a sovereign State. Our draft calls for full cooperation with the Mission, for maximum restraint by all Member States, and for respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It is balanced, realistic and aimed at preventing further escalation. We urge all members to support it. Russia will vote in favour.
before.Sweden: Mr. President, Sweden condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons and fully supports an immediate, independent and impartial OPCW investigation into the reported attack in Douma. But the Council’s response must also ensure accountability and uphold the demands of resolution 2401 (2018). The draft before us does not establish an independent mechanism to identify those responsible, and it weakens the Council’s demands for implementation of resolution 2401. Sweden will therefore vote against this draft. We remain ready to work with all members on a credible and effective response to this grave situation.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom has engaged constructively on this text, but we cannot support the draft as presented. We strongly condemn the use of chemical weapons in Douma. This is a violation of international law that must be investigated and those responsible must be held accountable. The Russian text still refers only to “reports” and “grave concern,” rather than clearly affirming that chemical weapons were used. It also fails to ensure that the OPCW investigation collects evidence relevant to accountability. Most seriously, it calls on all Member States to refrain from action that could escalate tensions — language that would constrain the response to chemical weapons and shield those responsible. Our core concerns have not been met. The United Kingdom will vote against this draft. We remain fully committed to an independent OPCW investigation and to holding accountable all those who use chemical weapons.
before.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft. The reported chemical weapons attack in Douma is a serious violation of international law, and the Council must respond with a credible, independent investigation that can identify those responsible. This text would instead constrain the Council, weaken accountability, and restrict the very access investigators need. Russia has repeatedly used this Council to shield the Syrian regime from consequences, and the United States will not join a resolution that fails to meet the gravity of the moment. We vote against.

after.Equatorial Guinea:
Mr. President,

The Republic of Equatorial Guinea voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation and wishes to explain that vote. We condemn, in the strongest terms, any use of chemical weapons, anywhere and by anyone. The reports concerning Douma are grave and must be clarified through a prompt, independent, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We supported this draft because it called for such an investigation, urged all parties to cooperate fully and without obstruction, reaffirmed the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and called for restraint by all Members, including against unilateral military action that could further escalate tensions.

We deeply regret that the Council has not been able to adopt this draft. At this dangerous juncture, division in the Security Council does not serve the cause of peace or the protection of civilians. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, to avoid any escalation, and to allow safe, unimpeded and sustained humanitarian access throughout Syria. Resolution 2401 (2018) must be fully implemented. Equatorial Guinea remains committed to a political solution to the Syrian crisis under the auspices of the United Nations, in full respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria. We urge the Council to continue its efforts to speak with one voice and to act responsibly.

Thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,
The Russian Federation regrets that the Security Council has failed to adopt a balanced and objective draft resolution on the reports of chemical weapons use in Douma. Our text was not aimed at shielding anyone. It called for an immediate, independent, impartial investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, for full cooperation with that Mission, and for the facts to be established without pre-judgment. It also demanded maximum restraint and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

We note the support of those members who voted in favour. At the same time, we regret that a number of delegations chose to vote against a text whose core purpose was a professional OPCW investigation. Their explanations confirm that what they sought was not truth but a predetermined conclusion and an open-ended mechanism to assign blame. Attempts to use this tragic event to push for unilateral military action and to undermine the political process are unacceptable and dangerous.

Russia will continue to insist that any investigation be conducted on the basis of reliable evidence and in full respect for Syrian sovereignty and international law. We call on all parties to cooperate with the OPCW and warn against any actions that could further escalate the situation in Syria and the region. The Council must remain seized of the matter and act responsibly.
after.Sweden: Mr. President, Sweden regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt a credible response to the deeply alarming reports of chemical weapons use in Douma. We voted against the draft because it did not provide for an independent mechanism to identify those responsible and would have weakened the implementation of resolution 2401 (2018). The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable under any circumstances and must never go unpunished. Sweden calls for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to be deployed without delay, with immediate, safe and unimpeded access, and for all parties to cooperate fully. The Council must also insist on the full implementation of resolution 2401, including cessation of hostilities, humanitarian pauses, medical evacuations and safe access to all besieged and hard-to-reach areas. The Council cannot remain divided in the face of such grave violations. Sweden remains ready to work with all members on a credible, evidence-based and effective response that upholds accountability and the protection of civilians.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom voted against this draft because it was not a credible response to the chemical weapons attack in Douma. The use of chemical weapons is a violation of international law and cannot be met with equivocation. The Council must insist on a genuinely independent investigation with immediate, unfettered access, and it must be prepared to hold those responsible accountable. The Russian text would have weakened those demands and constrained the Council’s ability to respond. Its failure is not a defeat for accountability; it is a rejection of an inadequate text. The United Kingdom will continue to work with partners to uphold the Chemical Weapons Convention, to support the OPCW, and to ensure that the perpetrators of chemical weapons use are identified and held to account. The Syrian regime and its backers must understand that the world will not look away.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President, the United States voted against this text, and the Council has rightly refused to endorse a resolution that would have shielded the Assad regime rather than held it accountable. The draft referred to the horrific attack in Douma only in terms of “reports.” It did not establish a credible mechanism to identify those responsible. And it included language calling on Member States to refrain from action — language that would constrain the Council at the very moment firmness is required.

The United States fully supports an immediate, independent, and impartial OPCW investigation, with safe and unimpeded access to all relevant locations. But an investigation that is not allowed to establish responsibility, and a Council that is told to look away, is not accountability. It is a roadmap for impunity.

We also insist on the full implementation of resolution 2401, including humanitarian access and the protection of civilians. The United States will not accept a text that weakens those obligations or gives cover to those who use chemical weapons against innocent men, women, and children.

Let us be clear: the United States will not allow the failure of this draft to become a license for further chemical weapons use. We will continue to work with our partners on a serious and credible response. If the Security Council cannot act, the United States will. The victims of Douma deserve better than the empty words and cynical maneuvers we have heard today.
